bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical instability (West Asia) causing raw material volatility and supply chain disruptions; Potential demand moderation in H2FY27 if price hikes are not fully passed through; Trade uncertainty in Mexico (US tariffs, USMCA review); Intense competition from new entrants in TBR/PCR segments.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and aggressive on growth (record volumes, massive capex commitment) but cautious on near-term margins due to external macro shocks; Emphasizes operational discipline, premiumization, and digital transformation (AI) as key moats.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly highlighted 'Agentic AI' deployment for decision-making and workflow automation, moving beyond basic analytics; The 'Selling Miles' fleet management program is positioned as a significant entry barrier against new competitors by creating service-based stickiness rather than just product sales; Mexico subsidiary (JK Tornel) facing sluggishness due to US tariff uncertainty despite stable full-year revenue.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Pioneer of radial tyre technology in India with a long-standing technology-led positioning
- Extensive pan-India distribution — ~900 outlets, 6,000+ dealer partners, 700+ dealer additions during the year, covering over 90% of India by geography
- Smart/connected-tyre technology via the TREEL platform — India's first embedded smart passenger car tyres, ~11 million data points/month
- Majority share in the EV bus segment with OEM-accepted EV-specific tyres (Jetway JUXe)
- Strong brand and motorsport-led positioning (Levitas, Guinness World Record drift, Formula 2-winning protege driver)
- Retreading network (JK Treads, 90+ centres, 450+ customers) extending tyre life and lowering customer cost per kilometre
- In-house R&D capability via the Raghupati Singhania Centre of Excellence (RPSCOE), Mysuru
- Diversified international manufacturing base in Mexico (JK Tornel) providing access to American markets
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and global trade uncertainty — The tyre industry's global integration exposes raw-material sourcing and export access to geopolitical shocks and trade protectionism (higher tariffs, instability), bringing supply-chain disruption and demand volatility that could slow the post-pandemic economic recovery.
- Raw material cost and supply volatility (crude-linked inputs) — Crude-linked raw material prices saw heightened volatility toward the end of FY26 due to geopolitical upheavals, including a March 2026 Strait of Hormuz-linked disruption, directly straining the global supply landscape and cost stability.
- Natural rubber supply deficit — A critical Natural Rubber deficit of 35% still persists in India; the Company's multi-year 'Inroad Project' rubber-plantation initiative in Northeast India (now in its fifth year) only partially bridges the domestic supply-demand gap, leaving continued reliance on imports.
- Export / international trade exposure — International business is shaped by trade protectionism, tariff uncertainty and geopolitical volatility, requiring a selective, region-led, margin-conscious export strategy (pricing discipline, receivable security) rather than volume-led growth.
- IT and cybersecurity risk — As digital integration deepens across manufacturing, customer interfaces, service systems and connected-product platforms, information security and system reliability become more material risk domains for the enterprise.
- Competitive intensity in the tyre industry — JK Tyre operates in a competitive industry facing multiple risks across financial, operational, sectoral, ESG, IT and cyber domains that could impact operations and financial performance, requiring sustained cost control, strategic diversification and R&D investment to mitigate.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Sweat existing/matured manufacturing assets to high utilisation (crossed 90% in key segments) before layering on fresh growth capex
- Premiumisation-led mix improvement across PCR, farm, truck/bus and 2/3-wheeler segments, including higher rim-size and performance-tyre participation
- Selective, margin-focused international growth — in JK Tornel (Mexico) export decisions are guided by profitability and portfolio discipline rather than headline volume, avoiding price-led competition against low-cost global substitutes
- Scale the connected/smart-tyre mobility platform (TREEL) — embedding sensing and data intelligence into tyres for safety and performance monitoring
- Shift from product-led selling to integrated lifecycle fleet management in Truck & Bus, via the Mobility Solutions platform and digital fleet-service interventions
- R&D-led material innovation aimed at decoupling growth from resource intensity — expanding sustainable/circular material usage (e.g., UX Green tyres made with 80% sustainable material) broadly across product categories rather than a few flagship SKUs, while preserving performance
- Expand rural distribution footprint via a new Rural Business vertical and Rural Distributor appointments into previously unrepresented markets
- Deepen pan-India channel network through dealer additions and branded retail/Steel Wheels outlet expansion
- In Mexico, strengthen domestic distribution, sharpen product mix and expand capacity ahead of demand as a structural response to tariff and currency volatility
- Digital-first, measurement-led brand building with sharper segment-specific communication across passenger, truck and farm categories
- The Board reviews long-term strategy and growth roadmap, capital expenditure plans and funding mix, risk management frameworks and sustainability targets/disclosures as part of its oversight. During the year, governance focus centred on capital efficiency (monitoring commissioning and ramp-up of newly installed capacities and ensuring targeted utilisation levels), debt optimisation (replacing higher-cost borrowings with lower-cost and foreign-currency debt while maintaining liquidity buffers), and risk preparedness for raw-material volatility, trade-tariff disruptions and capacity constraints through proactive planning. Board deliberations emphasised operational leverage, margin resilience and balance-sheet strength, ensuring growth initiatives remain aligned with financial prudence. The Notice of the AGM includes an item to declare a dividend, though no payout ratio or per-share figure is present in this text bundle.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Manufacturing focus shifted during the year from capacity creation to capacity optimisation, with recent investments across PCR, TBR and all-steel LCV radial driving stronger utilisation, throughput and mix quality. Phase III of the Banmore passenger car radial expansion was inaugurated on 14th January 2026, raising Banmore capacity to 30,000 tyres per day (about 10.5 million tyres annually). Expansion projects with a ₹1,400 crore outlay — the Banmore PCR expansion and the Laksar Truck Bus Radial (TBR) expansion — were commissioned during the year and are currently under ramp-up, with full utilisation expected by Q1 FY 2026-27. Capacity building also continued via all-steel radial additions and Mexico (JK Tornel) plant modernisation. In Mexico, JK Tornel initiated a US$75 million expansion programme (Phase I: US$27.5 million) to add ultra-modern manufacturing machines including uniformity systems, a new northern warehouse focused on over-16-inch rim-size tyres, and an expanded high-margin ATV portfolio; Phase I is scheduled for completion by July 2026. On the raw-material side, natural-rubber localisation is being advanced through Project INROAD, with nearly 90% of identified North-East plantations showing progress and production expected to begin from mid-2030.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic demand tailwind from India's GDP growth (over 7% in FY26, expected to remain above 6% in FY27), infrastructure/Gati Shakti capex and GST 2.0 rate rationalisation, which cut GST on Commercial Vehicles, small cars and tractors and had a positive rub-off on OEM tyre demand
- Indian tyre industry recorded double-digit growth in FY26 and is expected to roughly quadruple over the next two decades in line with the 'Viksit Bharat 2047' vision, supported by a large vehicle base, logistics/e-commerce growth, infrastructure expansion, premiumisation and radialisation
- Growth remained largely domestic/aftermarket-led; exports faced headwinds from tariff uncertainty, geopolitical volatility, logistics disruptions and high freight costs
- Raw material cost risk: inputs (over 60% of tyre cost) depend on imported natural and synthetic rubber; volatility rose toward year-end on a depreciating Rupee and higher crude prices, and the long-standing inverted duty structure remains unresolved
- FY27 industry outlook is positive but with moderate growth; material input costs are likely to escalate and new regulatory norms (CAFE III, BS7, TREM V) are likely to add further cost pressure over the long run
- Elevated geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia war) is an emerging headwind showing early signs of moderating growth
- Premiumisation and radialisation continue as structural demand drivers — SUV mix shift in PVs, entry-level to premium shift in 2W, and EV penetration doubling to ~4% in PVs and reaching ~7% in 2W
- Commercial vehicle segment demand supported by infrastructure projects, GST 2.0 logistics streamlining and scrappage-policy enforcement; bus electrification rising, led by State Transport Undertakings
- In Mexico, tariff and currency volatility are treated as a now-structural feature of global trade, prompting a deliberate emphasis on domestic distribution strength, product-mix sharpening and capacity built ahead of demand
- JK Tornel (Mexico) commenced OE supplies to Kia Mexico during the year, with additional SKUs planned, extending its OEM relationship pipeline in the North American market

deepdive.thesis: JK Tyre delivered record FY26 profitability with 270 bps margin expansion in Q4 driven by volume growth and mix, but faces immediate Q1FY27 headwinds from an 18-20% raw material cost surge due to geopolitical tensions. Management is countering this with staggered price hikes and committing to a massive Rs 6,110 crore capex plan through FY29 to alleviate >90% capacity utilization, signaling strong confidence in long-term structural demand despite short-term inflationary noise.

verdicts.note: EBITDA margin in Q4 were recorded at 12.9% versus 10.2% in Q4 of FY25, representing an expansion of 270 basis points, and for the full year, EBITDA margin stood at 12.8%.

verdicts.item: JK Tornel Q4 (Jan-Mar) revenue expected to recover from Q3 low (16 Christmas plant closure days); 95% of exports protected from US tariff uncertainty.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: TBR and PCR replacement identified as the two key growth segments for FY26; PCR replacement grew 24% YoY and overall replacement 16% YoY in Q3.
verdicts.note: TBR volumes in replacement market grew by 19% and OE market by 53% YoY. Passenger line volumes grew by 16% YoY, contributed by replacement at 10% and OE at 26%.

verdicts.item: Management guides to high-single-digit to double-digit consolidated revenue growth in FY26, led by replacement and new capacities.
verdicts.note: We delivered record volumes across segments, attaining the highest ever annual consolidated revenue of Rs.16,384 crore, a healthy double-digit growth of 11%.

verdicts.item: Rs.1,400 crore PCR/TBR/ASLTR projects to yield available capacities within FY26; ~Rs.900 crore capex outlay planned for FY26.
verdicts.note: Installed capacities were fully utilized across segments and for the full year at India level, the utilization was recorded at above 90%.

verdicts.item: JK Tornel FY26 performance and margins expected to be better than FY25, aided by zero US tariff on Mexican tyres and better mix.
verdicts.note: EBITDA in FY26 stood at Rs.141 crores and PBT grew by 63% to Rs.61 crores, while PAT grew by 91% to Rs.42 crores over the previous year.

verdicts.item: Full-year FY26 guided to initial double-digit growth, better than FY25, led by replacement.
verdicts.note: We delivered record volumes across segments, attaining the highest ever annual consolidated revenue of Rs.16,384 crore, a healthy double-digit growth of 11%.
